title: Disposition
description: Per-session structured outcome record. Mirrors ai_router/disposition.py::Disposition. Cross-field rules that depend on the closing session being final-or-not are enforced by validate_disposition() in code rather than by this schema, since 'is the final session' is not a property of the document itself.

verification_qualification.description: Set 123 S2, omit-null. Present only when the verdict beside it is real but WEAKER than the cross-provider standard: 'same-provider' means every verifier call resolved to the orchestrator's own effective provider, so the verdict is not independently corroborated. Written by verify_session (and the close backstop) for a project whose committed verify type is DIRECT_API and which holds no usable API key outside its orchestrator's provider. The vocabulary is CLOSED and fails closed -- unlike verification_verdict, whose non-canonical tokens are warned-but-accepted, an unrecognized qualification is a validation error, because a token nobody can interpret does this field's only job (letting a later reader tell a corroborated verdict from an uncorroborated one) worse than no token at all. The authoritative copy is the paired metrics stamp row, where the close gate enforces it as a bijection against the verifier's registry-resolved provider.

uat.description: Set 111 S4 (added to this schema in Set 130 S3). How a requiresUAT session discharged its guided-look walk. The uat_walk_recorded close gate reads it; a session that owes a walk and carries no block does not close. Omit-null on sets that declare no UAT. It was omitted here when it shipped, so this schema rejected -- under additionalProperties: false -- exactly the dispositions the gate requires.

checklist.description: Set 114 S1 (added to this schema in Set 130 S3). The operator-attested waiver for a step-checklist post that was missed. status is closed to 'waived' -- the block exists only to put a name against an omission; a session that posted on cadence needs no block, because the ledger already proves it.

Cost.description: Set 130 S3. What the session cost, by component, with a per-component status. Produced by seat_cost.CostReport.to_cost_block(); ai_router/docs/seat-cost.md is canonical for the three measurements and for the rule this shape encodes -- a report must say which measurement it is showing and name what it could not measure. Three cross-field rules below are the contract rather than shape, and each is also enforced by validate_disposition() so the two halves cannot drift (project-guidance Code Style: validator/schema parity in BOTH directions). One rule is validator-only because draft 2020-12 cannot express it: a component name may not appear twice.

measured_at.description: 'close' = taken by the session about itself, whose closing turns are not in the store yet, so the figure is a floor. 'retrospective' = taken afterwards, exact.

store_schema_version.description: The local usage store's schema_version the number was read against, or null when nothing was read. The store path itself is deliberately NOT carried here: it is an absolute path on one operator's machine and this artifact is committed.

allOf.description: Rule 2: a report containing an unmeasured component has no total. A total that quietly drops one reports unmeasured spend as zero.
Rule 3: an as-of-close figure cannot claim to be exact (spec T5 -- a session cannot measure itself).

CostComponent.description: One separately-labelled component. Rule 1 lives here: credits and usd are null for every non-numeric status, because 0.0 beside status 'unknown' reads as a measurement and a later reader cannot tell it from a real zero (L-112-1).
